literal: Within wealth, poverty is the folly of not practicing hospitality to guests, which exists with the foolish.
translation: Poverty amidst wealth is the folly of not practicing hospitality to guests; such ignorance is found only among the foolish.
modern: செல்வத்திற்குள் வறுமை என்பது விருந்தினரை உபசரிக்காத அறியாமை ஆகும்; இந்த அறியாமை அறிவற்ற மூடர்களிடம் மட்டுமே இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet redefines poverty not as a lack of material wealth, but as the failure to share it. The poet states that possessing great wealth yet failing to practice hospitality is equivalent to being poor while rich. This failure is described as a form of ignorance or folly. Such foolish behavior is found only among those who lack true wisdom and understanding.
